text:
They drive their pulsating presence

into a gold wearied by ash,

dark birds rocking

on the back of trembling water.


Their throats heap up silences,

their wings lie inert at their flanks.

No eyes to look at them, no brow

to think of them. Only birds.


The hour is ending. Everything ends

or everything is about to begin… If it were known

that ending and beginning are the same,

perhaps this present would yield us


the almond of its light, would give us

the pulp of knowing why we came;

whether we are chosen by other worlds

or their slaves, fated


to give ourselves as sustenance for their life.

The gold is an absence, the ash

answers the tireless assault…

The eternal gathers in its lair.

translation.title: They Drive Their Pulsating Presence...
translation.editorial_note: The translation retains the stark birds, the suspended question of ending and beginning, and the poem’s final return to the eternal’s ‘manida,’ its lair.
